{"id": "2712e0e5-1de0-447d-b1d7-adc862f04338", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Yes, the storage never expires, but at the moment it costs almost nothing.

**What I found**
- Invocation logs go to the CloudWatch log group `/llmops-demo/bedrock-invocations`. There is no S3 destination.
- **The log group has no retention policy**, so it is set to "never expire". Every log event stays until someone deletes it.
- It was created around 2026-10-15 and holds about 124 MB (124,494,376 bytes).
- Text and video data delivery are on. Image and embedding delivery are off.

**Cost**
- That is roughly 3 MB a day over the last ~40 days, or about 1 GB a year at the current rate.
- At CloudWatch Logs storage pricing (about $0.03 per GB-month, from memory, so check current pricing), storage costs well under a cent a month today.
- Ingestion is the larger charge. It is billed once per GB when the logs are written, at about $0.50 per GB for Standard class. Retention doesn't change it.
- The growth is linear and would only become a real cost if your Bedrock traffic or payload sizes increase a lot. Video delivery or large prompts could do that.

**Recommendation**
Set a retention period on the log group, for example 30, 90 or 365 days, depending on your audit and debugging needs. If you need longer-term retention, an S3 destination with a lifecycle rule is usually cheaper than keeping everything in CloudWatch.

If you tell me the retention period you want, I can apply it to the log group. You would need to approve the change before it runs.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
